title: My theory…
content: There is something about the unique vast, public structure of a mall that resonates in the unconscious of people almost universally. Same with schools and other large labyrinth-type interiors. It had to have been a MUCH more profound experience than we realize to experience these huge, stimulating spaces for the first time as a kid. The resonance never really goes away subconsciously. When we dream, our brain transforms abstract thoughts & emotions into visual, spacial & tactile forms. It pulls from our personal trove of visual, spatial & tactile memories to create this dream world. I think the “trauma” of going from our small, cloistered home world as little kids to a space so MASSIVE and overstimulating for the first time makes a huge impact on our developing brain. Having our baby self’s notion of the world’s size & safety BLOW UP like that must have been profoundly frightening or exhilarating at a deep level we don’t fully remember or comprehend. But it’s still there, unconsciously, so our brain continues to use the space to convey anxiety or wonder in adulthood.
